HOUSE PUSHES ₱1B FUNDING FOR PROJECT NOAH

The House of Representatives on Saturday urged its Senate counterparts to consider allocating ₱1 billion for the Nationwide Operational Assessment of Hazards (Project NOAH) during the bicameral conference committee deliberations on the proposed 2026 national budget.

Negros Occidental 3rd District Rep. Javier Miguel Lopez Benitez backed the proposal, stressing Project NOAH's critical role in providing real-time, high-quality hazard maps that are used by local government units nationwide.

"Project NOAH has made real-time, high-quality hazard maps (which) has been used by local government units," Benitez said. "Ever since nangyayari po sa ating ang mga climate disasters, the (Project NOAH) website has had 35 million searches online; during peak times, 2.5 million searches a day."

Benitez said the surge in demand for accurate flood information—especially during impending typhoons—underscores the need to update hazard maps nationwide. He noted that Project NOAH's hazard maps were last comprehensively updated in 2012.

The lawmaker is among the authors of House Bill No. 2577, which seeks to establish the National Climate Resilience Institute under the University of the Philippines (UP) system.

House Committee on Appropriations Chairperson and Nueva Ecija 1st District Rep. Mika Suansing also pushed for the proposed funding, framing it as part of broader efforts to mitigate flooding and improve disaster preparedness.

"Ang hinihingi po natin sa Project NOAH kapag binigay natin ang pondo na ito is for them to work closely with the DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways) in terms of refining the way flood control projects are designed and monitored," Suansing said.

She explained that Project NOAH's modeling tools can simulate specific areas to determine precisely where flood control structures should be built.

"Hindi na po magkakaroon ng pagkakataon na makapaglagay ng flood control project sa lugar na hindi naman talaga kailangan lagyan," she added.

Suansing also noted that Project NOAH's annual budget has sharply declined over the years—from around ₱500 million to just ₱36 million—despite the project's continued production of reliable hazard maps relied upon by millions of Filipinos.

Project NOAH is currently implemented by the UP National Resilience Institute.
